name: TACIT
description: Theory-anchored qualitative coding with interpretive transparency. A Streamlit application that codes interview transcripts against a pluggable theoretical framework, keeps interpretive authority with the researcher, and reports the agreement statistics a qualitative study is expected to report. Coding frameworks can be constructed from literature retrieved via OpenAlex, with a guard that rejects citations absent from the retrieved corpus and per-dimension researcher approval. Model coding is treated as a draft: the model's original judgement is retained alongside every researcher revision, so the correction rate is reportable. Inter-rater reliability is computed over a sampling frame that includes unmarked units, so model recall is estimable. Language models may be served locally (Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp, vLLM, any OpenAI-compatible endpoint) so that transcripts need not leave the researcher's machine.

affiliation.name: Institute of Technology Management, National Yang Ming Chiao Tung University

softwareRequirements.name: google-genai
softwareRequirements.description: Google Gemini provider. Installed with the requirements so that Gemini works without a local model server. Local providers use the Python standard library.

softwareRequirements.name: plotly
softwareRequirements.description: Charts. Without it the interface falls back to tables.

softwareRequirements.name: scipy
softwareRequirements.description: Chi-square tests and Cramer's V. Without it those statistics are disabled and the rest of the analysis is unaffected.

softwareRequirements.name: ckip-transformers
softwareRequirements.description: Traditional Chinese word segmentation. Installed by the launchers as a separate step because it pulls in PyTorch; without it the lexicon module falls back to an n-gram heuristic.

referencePublication.name: TACIT: an auditable, locally-deployable Python tool for LLM-assisted qualitative coding with codebook provenance
